observations.location: Security Signal Review › Data Protection and Collaboration › evidence table › row: Forwarding block 0/5; mailbox auditing 0/3, To address › CIS Microsoft 365 Benchmark column
observations.detail: Evidence-status wording is inconsistent across tables: 'Not assessed' appears in the endpoint, cloud workload, and AI tables; 'CIS not tested' appears in the identity table; and 'Exact CIS configuration not assessed' appears in this row and the calendar-sharing row. The draft does not establish that these labels carry different meanings.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › AI Agents and Generative AI Usage › closing paragraph
observations.detail: The paragraph states that 'the awareness guidance in this report addresses verification of impersonation attempts', but the Security Awareness call-out in Recommended Security Actions addresses cloud misconfiguration and shadow API exposure. Impersonation verification is referenced only in the Recommendation History advisory table for Q1.

observations.location: Security Signal Review › Data Protection and Collaboration › closing paragraph
observations.detail: The paragraph lists five actions (the three continuing recommendations, attachment filtering, forwarding review, active DLP implementation, and calendar and Teams restrictions) and states they correspond to Active Recommendations 1 through 4, but active DLP implementation is not named in any Active Recommendation row; DLP appears only in the CIS benchmark table entry 2.1.2; 3.2.1.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Active Recommendations › Status column; Recommended Security Actions › CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark › Status column
observations.detail: The template specifies the status format 'MM.DD.YYYY - <STATUS DESCRIPTION>'; the draft supplies quarter-level labels such as '2026 Q3: All three remain To address.' without per-item dates.

observations.location: Recommended Security Actions › Security Awareness call-out
observations.detail: The template presents Security Awareness as a bolded call-out paragraph; the draft renders it as a single-column table produced by document conversion. Content and facts are unchanged.
